Really nice step up from FC24! As an avid enjoyer of the FIFA games for the past decade, it adds much more depth in realism and the animations are really fluid. Furthermore, its nice to see that they have made more platform stability changes and bug free initial launch patches especially since FC24 was really buggy compared to FC25 when I first bought it. I'm not saying it doesn't have bugs, but it definitely has a lot less. The new player career mode has a new GUI interface and is much more appeasing to the eye. Would say the career mode is the best change in this FIFA aside from the RUSH 5V5 mode. Haven't tried Manager Career Mode yet, but it looks really fun from the content I have watched. But you should consider buying it on discounts only, since it makes it more value for money for people for FC24 OR FIFA23 to upgrade. I wouldn't say there is a vast difference though, since its fundamentals are the same, but a few new additions like tactics and some human errors during a pass or shooting might be annoying to adjust to. TL;DR - This game is a psychologically manipulative Skinner box. It is designed to be addictive, and to get as much money out of you as possible. Scripting, implemented to encourage FUT players to spend more money, is in every mode and makes every game an unsatisfying and empty experience. Considering a core demographic for this game is children, the income-focused manipulation displayed here is repugnant.DDA (dynamic difficulty adjustment) or scipting is just ridiculous now. In games against EA's garbage AI, if the game wants your opponent to score, they'll respond to your controller inputs instantly, not the actions of the player you're controlling. Easy tackles with world class defenders will either miss, bounce the ball to another opponent, just outright phase through the ball or even the damn player! Your keeper will do a Matrix-esque dodge of a shot coming directly at them or will spill an easy catch directly into their striker. The most outrageous though, is player switching on loose balls and when contesting headers. The game will sometimes prevent you from switching to a player (even manually with the right stick) if they're close enough to win a loose ball or are in the best position to win a header. They will instead just stand there, staring blankly into the distance, until the opponent wins back possession. It's the most obvious example of the game cheating to achieve the outcome it wants. This stuff is so obvious that I've been able to predict when a goal is coming, just by how many advantages the AI gets.Other examples:- 30 year old fullback with 60 pace will gain an otherworldly burst of speed to get ahead of my winger with 90 pace- Players will frequently and deliberately place themselves in a position to lose headers, even if you're instructing them to do the opposite- Opposition defenders will basically teleport to tackle you the second you press shoot in the box- Your passes will frequently go to a player in the complete opposite direction to the one you've commanded- Uncontrolled defenders will randomly clatter someone in the box, giving away a penalty- Some of the AI's most outrageous Sunday league fouls just won't be given- If the game doesn't want you to score anymore (or has the scoreline it wants to achieve), the opposition will just pass the ball around the back or run all the way back to the keeper upon any pressure. This would be fine if they weren't 2-1 down at 70', where any team would be pushing hard for an equaliser. Again, just breaks the immersion.- If the game wants you to score, all of these advantages are removed and opposing players lose 50 IQ points. It's ridiculously transparent.These problems extend to all other game modes, especially Ultimate Team.At the end of the day, all this does is damage the experience. Wins don't feel earned, since it's obvious that the game is allowing you to win. When you lose it's often because of the above advantages, not from been legitimately outplayed. For a game that aims to recreate football, it fails spectacularly in presenting the core part of that experience; the in-match gameplay. Neglecting this, by adding a scripting or variable difficulty system to psychologically manipulate FUT players to spend more money, not only irrevocably destroys the experience in all modes, but is also outrageously anti-consumer. I knew on reputation that EA Sports games were microtransaction ridden hellholes but this is predatory to a degree I've never seen before. Considering a core demographic for this game is children, manipulation like this is repugnant. Honestly, I feel dirty having spent money on this.Do not buy this or any other EA Sports Skinner box, it's a prime example of everything wrong with this heinous company.

Sorry you can't as there are no 433 formations with this midfield combinationIf you want to make an asymmetric formation (like having a LW with a RM)? Sorry you can't as the preset formations provided are all symmetric and standard formationsIf you want to make adjustments during a match? Sorry you can't adjust the position of players (player positions cannot be adjusted (like making a CM to CAM when you are losing), only the very limited attacking instructions and overall formation can be changedIf your defence is under great pressure? Sorry your LM/RM/CM/CAM won't help the defence and will stand still and watch the ball on the midfield as the IQ thinks the jobs of the midfield players are only for the midfield (no options on defending behaviours)If you are having a clear and potential chance of one-on-one opportunity? Sorry even if your CAM/CM is next to you, he may stand still as he belongs to the midfield)Inconsistent gameplay and possible scripting (I play 10 min half time, and I have experienced this frequently - during a match if I score, then the speed of the player movement and the ball, as well as the action of every player will be boosted suddenly, and my sliders will no longer apply, and the AI will pass the ball very quickly and score easily as your defenders will just stand still without tracing the attackers and your GK will just dive on the ground without saving it even it should be a easy save)Unfair game with the AIWhen the AI defends. for many teams, their midfielders and defenders will have a very compact defence shape (they may even get speed boost when they tackle you) But for your own team, only defenders are defending, even sometimes they just stand still and watch the ball (For attacking it is in similar scenario) (Kind of intentional design by the game)It is also easy to end up with abusing one-two through pass/dribbling as your players won't move(strikers frequently end up in stupid positions of the box like moving slowly far behind you/do't appear in empty space)I have also experienced a lot of bugs/crashes/screen freezes, especially in half time/between the end of a match and the start of the press conference that I cannot do anything but close the game directly and lose all the progress (I have no problems playing other AAA games in high settings)Disclaimer: I have tried and applied no sliders/preset in-game sliders provided and many popular sliders provided by online communities, and I have only played career mode games in legendary difficulty (I heard that world class might provide a more realistic experience but it is too easy for me to win), so what you might experience can be differentFC IQ tactics is a good try/starting point in my opinion but too far from finished product which mimics realistic tactics in real life football

"FIFA 25 Review: A Solid Football Experience for Fans, But Is It Worth the Full Price?"FIFA 25 is an impressive football experience that caters well to fans of the sport. ⚽ Overall, the game has a lot going for it, especially for those who are passionate about football and seek the thrill of managing and competing with their favorite teams and players. However, the question remains: is it worth the full price without a discount?Gameplay and OptimizationOne of the first things I noticed about FIFA 25 is that it feels smoother and more optimized compared to previous versions. 🖥️ Whether you’re playing on high-end or mid-range hardware, the game runs more efficiently and provides a better experience overall. That’s a big improvement and a welcome change, as past versions have often had performance issues that were frustrating for players.Learning CurveIf you're new to the FIFA series, brace yourself: the initial stages can be tough. 📈 There’s a lot to learn, and mastering the controls and tactics requires time and practice. But don’t let that discourage you! The training modes are well-designed, and with a bit of patience, you'll find yourself progressing. Soon enough, you'll start pulling off those satisfying goals and clever plays, but expect to invest time in practice.Monetization and Luck FactorOne aspect where FC 25 faces mixed reviews is its monetization. As with previous games, you can buy packs that may give you an advantage if you land strong players. 💸 The luck of the draw means you could get top-tier players that provide a big edge in gameplay, which can feel a bit unfair at times. For players willing to spend extra on packs, there is a clear advantage. However, the game is still playable without spending, though it may require a lot more grinding and strategic play.Comparison to Previous VersionsWhile FIFA 25 has made strides in certain areas, there are still parts where it feels like it hasn’t evolved as much as expected. Some gameplay mechanics are definitely smoother, and there’s a bit more polish, but you may not feel a huge leap forward if you’re coming from FIFA 24. For longtime players, the differences may be a bit subtle, which can be both a positive and a negative depending on your perspective.Final VerdictSo, is FC 25 worth getting? My advice is to grab it on sale, like I did. 🤑 While the improvements are notable, the full price feels a bit steep, especially for players who aren’t deeply invested in the series. With a discount, it’s a solid buy and can provide countless hours of fun, even if there are a few quirks and balancing issues with monetization. If you're a die-hard football fan, there’s a lot to enjoy, and you’ll likely appreciate the gameplay tweaks and improved optimization. Just be prepared for a challenge, especially if you’re new, and keep in mind that some players may gain an advantage through additional purchases.Overall Rating: Worth it on sale, maybe not at full price.

I can’t even comprehend how bad a video game can be, so here are my thoughts (mostly about Ultimate Team) as a pros/cons list.CONS:-Nontent every day; I can’t remember the last time they added a quality SBC that wasn’t either overpriced or just down right bad.- "Microtransactions" - packs cost €15-25 each; with new packs added daily, I assume that's what they call “content.”- There’s always at least one AFK player in rush games, since it’s the quickest way to complete evolutions. You can’t do anything about it, so you just carry on, struggling against tryhards on the opposing team. I wonder if they’ll ever add an option to kick AFK players.- There was no option to mute the commentator in Rush mode until they finally added it in a recent patch.- CPU defense is too strong. You’ll end up passing the ball around for 10-15 minutes, hoping your opponent will get impatient and rush their defender so you can finally score. The same issue exists in Squad Battles—sometimes, you’ll easily win on Legendary difficulty, while other times you’ll struggle to score and lose.- "Nonexistent" DDA - Even if your opponent is down 0-5 at halftime, they still have a high chance of making a comeback. EA, of course, claims there’s no such thing as Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment (DDA).- Player intelligence is poor; 80% of passes go off-target, so you end up losing possession. The defensive and attacking AI is lacking as well.- The game demands a huge time commitment. For better rewards, you’ll need to play 44 games a week (12 in Division Rivals, 15 in FUT Champions, 12 in Squad Battles, and 5 qualifiers), each lasting around 10 minutes. That’s 7 hours a week, which isn’t terrible, but realistically you’d need to play 20-25 games to achieve 12 wins in Division Rivals. While the rewards are better, they’re still not worth the time, which seems intended to push players toward store packs.- Many players do nothing but spam skill moves such as fake shots and roulettes, repeatedly losing possession. It’s repetitive and frustrating.- Running to the edge of the field, cutting back, and scoring is easy because the goalkeeper’s AI doesn’t react well.- The game crashes often after redeeming an SBC.- After every game, there’s a popup showing objective completion—even when nothing was actually completed.- Sometimes, the playstyle+ icon turns into large white triangles covering the screen, which requires you to restart the game for them to disappear.- Inviting friends to a lobby is unreliable, as the overlay button frequently disappears, forcing you to restart the game.- Draft hasn’t been updated in eight years, and they haven’t even adjusted offline match length to match that with Squad Battles.- Lack of highly advertised cosmetic evos.PROS:- You can create good-looking players in Clubs mode.- Manager mode is relatively well-rounded and enjoyable.- Roles+ and Roles++- Most Ultimate Team modes have updated rewardsSUMMARY:While the gameplay feels smoother than in FC24, the experience remains disappointing, especially with the push for microtransactions. Overall, I don’t recommend buying the game or spending money on packs.

This is my first ever review of a FIFA/EAFC game. I've been a dedicated player since 2015's instillation, having racked up hundreds of hours across the titles. EAFC25 is by far, the worst game from this franchise that I have ever played. This may be a little of a rant but I highly encourage any fans of previous titles to read this review before paying an absurd $70 for this cash grab of a game.Let's start with the most jarring issue I've run into - bugs and stability. Every time I boot up this game, it's 50/50 if a new audio or visual bug will appear, or if the game will simply crash when navigating the menus. I definitely don't have a super computer, but being able to run games like RDR2, Cyberpunk, etc. at ultra high should mean this game runs fine, but it doesn't. Now let's get into other areas...--Menus--Comparing the new menu setup in the EAFC titles compared to the FIFA ones shows a night and day difference of user friendly interface. The menu in EAFC25 is ugly, makes it a chore to navigate to different tabs, and will most likely cause your game to crash.I spend most of my time playing in career mode, which is where the faults of the menu system really shine. Need to adjust your team lineup? Go through 4 different menu selections. Need to see how your team is doing in league standings? Go through 4 different menu selections. Want to save your game with the press of a button? Nope, go find it at the very end of the menu under settings.--Gameplay--The gameplay this year is atrocious. Passing, running, defending, and simply switching players has become a complete point of frustration. Making the most simply passes now brings a 50/50 chance that the ball will go to the completely wrong player/area of the field. Trying to switch between players while defending has severe input delay and often goes to the wrong player. You no longer can use the thumb stick to switch to a specific player which means you're relying on the systems predictive capability.Crossing has become useless as the ball is so inconsistently delivered into the box, often having no pace or are sent behind a player making a run. Through balls and the CPU advanced runs have also become completely useless. Players making forward runs now either stop randomly, stay offsides, or become strangely hard to control once they receive the ball, resulting in a turnover. Defending now means its a 50/50 chance a successful tackle won't even move the ball away from the opposing player. Want to contest a player making a run? Nope, your player does a full stop standing tackle.While it seems like a cool idea to have a controlled sprint and a full sprint control, this has actual made dribbling/running extremely hard to predict and control. The Speed/Acceleration attributes of players has also become useless, as defenders with 50 pace easily out sprint a winger with 90 pace and 90 dribbling. Movement feels clunky, especially with skill moves and dribbling. There seems to be a severe input delay whenever trying to do a skill.Comparing this year's instillation to my most played title, FIFA 22, it seems that the gameplay has regressed in every way possible. The easiest way to describe how it feels playing this game is trying to shove a square peg into a round hole.--Other Misc. Issues--The matter of licensing rights with several Serie A teams has meant the creation of fake aliases for teams like Ac Milan, Napoli, and more. While this doesn't bother me that much, it feels like EA Sports simply doesn't care about providing a good product anymore. Along with the names being changed for the teams, they've been given new kits that look like a 5 year old designed them. It makes playing as these teams in career mode or online seasons very unattractive.There also seems to be a lack of production quality for any of the cutscenes before games, doing player/manager interviews, and more. The sound design for small things like cleats(boots) clacking in the locker room sounds awful, the options for interview questions haven't changed in 5 years, and the prematch analysis still gets player names/positions/performances wrong.--Some Positives--Banging soundtrack.--Summary--This game stinks, don't spend $70, or even $30+. You're better off purchasing previous year's titles and manually adjusting the rosters. For a studio that has limitless funds for yearly instilations, hardly anything has changed for the better.

I ruminated on whether or not the gameplay was actually sophisticated or just poorly optimized, and I decided that it was indeed badly designed. Over the past few years, EA have made many aspects of the game highly manual and specialized, to the extent that shooting effectively requires three buttons. Triggering runs is mostly manually done, dribbling is complicated, pressing is mostly manual, and so on. This may seem like sophisticated gameplay at first glance but once these mechanics are figured out, the resulting gameplay looks extremely unnatural and it is often more reliable to take finesse long shots over basic passing plays.Then of course there is the issue of how players are funnelled into the highly exploitative Ultimate Team, which was a fun concept until EA amped up the costs to get players that are useful in the game, and force you to do mind-numbing squad building challenges to get the advanced players. The neglected and highly unrealistic career modes are also frustrating to play due to the inane and one-dimensional objectives needed to progress or avoid being berated.I concede that Rush is a fun game mode, and the rewards are fairly distributed compared to other modes like squad battles. Rush mode is of course vulnerable to griefers and other selfish tendencies present in online gameplay, particularly because the rewards do not require performance and they can be afked to the frustration of the other players in the match. This is moreso a fault of basic humanity, a test which a worryingly large amount of people seem to fail.The Menu UI is also not great, and it takes what feels like ages to cycle through the myriad of different pages, which are also laggy due to the unnecessary high-fi player backgrounds for the main menu pages.It makes me nostalgic for the times when the game was consistently fun and addictive, now it is just frustrating and overly sweaty. It is lamentable that the video game industry has ceased to be a true free market and the games with the most investment are designed to extract as much revenue from its playerbase as possible, rather than delivering a quality product. How I miss pre-2008 capitalism!

This is a review of the Ultimate Team mode specifically. Player AI is also terrible; players will routinely put themselves where you can't pass to them. Ground passing is broken even on semi-assisted because the directionality is so random, and the pace of the ball on precision passing makes that almost unusable. Player switching even when using ball-relative right-stick switching can require up to three attempts to get the player you want. I could go on but you get the idea. I respect anyone who can be good at this game regardless, because it is utter jank. Then there is the change to the reward system which makes you get 15 wins for maximum rewards in Rivals. 15. I am writing this review right after my game crashed at the 89th minute. I have not crashed in-game in over a few yearsI played FC24 and found it fun and enjoyable to an extent. Not great per se, but not terrible either. I got this game thinking that it would at the very least be the same. But no, this game is significantly slower, has significantly more bugs and crashes, and has a massive hacking problem. On top of all that, communication from EA to the player base addressing bugs and glitches is almost nonexistent.Ultimate TeamRush, which was this game's only redeemable factor, has been ruined by selfish and/or AFK players that can ruin fun for others with no punishment, not to mention the fact that you will encounter the same unrewarding gameplay mechanics that plague the other game modes across the title.Evolutions , which were a revolutionary concept last year, has been riddled with bugs blocking valid evolution chains and removing stat upgrades for no reason. On a separate note, one paid evolution in particular had extremely absurd requirements, requiring 24 wins in a limited game mode.Squad battles has become much more difficult compared to previous titles. If you search for other players' experiences online or play a game yourself, you will find that playing World Class difficulty, for example, will be much more difficult than last year. Reaching 5 goals against WC difficulty AI used to be easy even with off-chem and silver teams, but the AI now plays with significantly higher pressing and in a much more possessive manner. AI-controlled slow defenders also seem to catch up to pacey wingers much more even when neither have the ball.has had the worst update out of all UT game modes. Previously, reward levels were at 4 and 7 wins. Now, they are at 5 and 15. Unless you are at a division much weaker than yourself, it will take quite some time reaching 15 wins. Even with better rewards, it is insane that the next reward upgrade from 5 wins is 15.qualifications now requires 3/5 wins compared to the previous 4/10, and finals consists of only 15 games. The new qualification requirement now forces out many players that would have made it through to the finals in the previous titles, resulting in a much sweatier finals experience for those that do make it through. On PC in particular, it will be near impossible to reach top rewards even for pros due to the absurdly high number of hackers.is riddled with bugs as well. Transfer ratings are nonsensical and weak foot/skill move upgrades are not reflected in game. Modding may be necessary to make these modes more enjoyable. Some objectives in the player career mode that give season points are also bugged and will not allow you to get the points for that objective and the objective group as a whole.shares some of the same issues with UT, notably with Rush. Matchmaking is also quite poor and there have been recorded instances of players loading into the game as players on the other team.In general, both you and your opponent will experience the following:- You do not win the ball after making a good tackle or you win the ball after making a good tackle and immediately lose it- You will get a red card and concede a penalty after making a good tackle- A player will be visibly and obviously offside, but a pass to that player will not be flagged as offside- Your goalkeeper will look away from the ball- You will concede a comically absurd power shot- You will be disconnected from a game while winning and be told that EA are looking at results to determine who won- Your goalkeeper will save a shot only for the ball to bounce straight to the feet of another opponent player for an easy goal- Your game will freeze in the menus- You will have a Rush teammate that is AFK all game and plays every opponent onside- Your player will miss an easy goal despite green timing the shot- Your pass will be misdirected to another player and the pass will be intercepted- You will lose a game despite having significantly more xG than the opponentIf you want to play a football game, I recommend sticking to any previous renditions of the game you already own or wait for other releases. Because until EA does something drastic, this game will not be enjoyable. The only reason why people will still play this game is because of FOMO and the fact that they paid 60 dollars for it.

[DISCLAIMER THIS IS A REVIEW FROM SOMEONE WHO PLAYS FUT PRIMARILY]Recommendation:(I havent played Fc/Fifa for 3yrs and have never been the greatest at the game, but I found to be able to achieve an own style of playing thats working for me)1. Since the Release I played an average of 8.5h a day (cooked) Can I recommened the Game ? For People who are bored and looking for a addicting game that wastes all your time, YES !2. If you have any other games to play that are fun or you havent played some of the greatest singleplayer games, you dont want to spend all your time on this game so, NO !>Gameplay<Is fun but NOT realisticMetas change constantly and new updates decide whether you have to change your players, tactic and formation.Menu and interfaces can be laggy and certain graphic settings can make your game crash.Playstyles are a insane feature that I love it just adds more variety and personality to the game.(if you just buy meta cards but dont use their playstyles ur not playing the game to its max. extend)Roles and Formations are wonky and dont work how their supposed to in some cases but it does the job (mostly!)Pack luck seems a bit rougher than usual which is fine I guess since the markets more stable. (I think)Season pass is a good feature and if you enjoy the other Fc Games modes you can get some levels ahead. (Can be boring but maybe youll enjoy some objectives/Modes)Rush is just mostly goofy and 1/3 of the playerbase is afk and people dont care about the rush objectives and if there is a season objective where you have to get assists have fun getting the ball passed in the worst situations since everbody just wants to quickly do their objectives (can be very fun with friends tho)Weekend League has gotten less grindy which i like its just more intense because of the lower amounts of games you can play. But the better rewards make up for it.Division Rivals hasnt really changed much for me.Squad Battles is very weird, they changed the ai with the update which completly threw me off while i was playing. Id say its harder but the less games makes it playable.For me I cant really say that i enjoy player career, manager or pro clubs.Player career is so repetitive and takes ages for some features like changing your club.Manager seems kinda fun but the old school manager was just simply better and is just to repetitive for me.>Fut Overall<Content is coming in at a good pace.Gameplay is frustrating since their are so many abusable shots and tricks right now.(getting slowly fixed tho)Market seems good and you have the feeling of impact when you start to actually have coins.Many people have almost the same Team (Thuram,Griezmann,etc.)And it can get very frustrating to always play against the same cards.You can have a very nice team for a low amount of coins since they added women which in combination with the newer chemistry system.Alot of Content if you are really down bad to do whatever it takes for cards and coins.I bought and I dont regret it since i havent had anything else to playTldr:6/10 Game with Crazy highs and lows and an insane amount of things to do that actual feel like your progressing.

EA FC 25 isn't just the second game by EA it's the worlds game.The game is more realistic than FC 24 having a completely overworked tactic management and different styles.You need to search for the matching players with certain play styles and player roles.Here are my plus and minus point about EA FC 25:+ It's realistic+ FC IQ (better tactical management)+ Rush (Rush replaces the former Volta Football mode with a 5 v 5 mode. It's perfect for playing with friends)+ New Walkout animations+ new GK play styles (including ++ GK play styles)- Volta Football got sadly removed (It was a very funny former mode)- The Career mode still misses an announced feature which allows you to start your career at the current game weeks- Only slight overworked Icon cards (there are some Icons I wouldn't rate as high as other Icons in comparison)Please note that this entire comment is my own oppinion and chances are high that you experience the game completely different than I am.Should you buy it?:If you already owned an EA FC or FIFA game I would of course recommend you FC 25, as you already got experience playing with its mechanics.If you're new to EA FC and want to buy it, I would also recommend it to you. EA FC 25 is a great game with cool graphics and it makes a lot of fun. Moreover, EA FC 25 has a pretty nice career and manager mode if you prefer to play offline with the newest transfers.If you decided to stop playing FIFA or EA FC I could understand it, as one of the most popular reasons being that this game is very competitive when playing online.If you like to play against friends or like to have a competition I would totally recommend EA FC 25 to you. There are a variety of different cool online modes like Clubs (If you prefer to play as one player in a team of AI's or Friends), Rush (a 5 v 5 mode where you got 6 min. to win as a team) and of course Division Rivals (your Ultimate Team playing against other Clubs trying to score as many wins and points to move up in the Divisions).I like to personally like to play with friends in Rush while having a big competition trying to rank up in Divisions. The new game mechanics are very nice and I would recommend you to try out this game, even if you aren't that into football.

Rating: 10/10(If only my wife rated our marriage as highly…)It all started innocently enough. “Oh, I’ll just play FC25 for an hour. What’s the harm in that, right?” I said to myself, blissfully unaware that I was already signing the death warrant for my marriage. Oh God, those were beautiful times—before I lost everything!Week One:FC25 is just a masterpiece! Gameplay so smooth, even Messi would be jealous. Goal after goal, dream team assembled, and I felt like the king of life. Everything around me ceased to exist—work? Who needs it! Wife? Still there! (At least, at the time.)Week Two:The anxiety kicks in. How is it possible that my team with Ronaldo, Mbappe, and Lewandowski keeps losing to some kid from Somalia with a squad made of last year’s leftovers? I blame the algorithms. It’s just not possible that, after two weeks of playing, I’m still stuck in the Bronze League. I start scratching myself in weird places, my wife asks what’s wrong with me. And me? I’m losing my mind because I can’t score from a corner kick.Wife starts to worry. “Honey, is it normal that you’ve been sitting at the console all day, haven’t showered in a week, and you’re singing the Champions League anthem while shaving?” she asks. With my eyes glued to the screen, I mutter: “This is my virtual season, babe! The fate of world football is at stake here!” She walks out of the room, and I score an own goal. Coincidence? I think not.We stop talking. The last time we exchanged words was when she accidentally sat on my controller. She was trying to help because I was in the middle of a complicated play. So, what did she do? Of course, she hit pause. And you can’t pause an online match! Boom! Game lost, promotion down the drain. That was the moment I realized FIFA had become more important than anything else in my life.It’s over. With my wife, obviously. She gave me an ultimatum—her or FIFA. It was the most nerve-wracking decision of my life, but in the end, I did what any true football fan would do: I bought a new controller. On her way out, she said, “Enjoy your FC25!” And I replied, “Oh, I will!” And that was the end. For her, at least. I’m still grinding my way to Division 1.FC25 is a world-class game! I’ve lost my wife, my sanity, and my connection to reality, but who cares—I’ve played the best virtual football of my life. If you dream of destroying your personal life and replacing it with an emotional rollercoaster, FC25 is the game for you. But be warned, when you’re left alone on the couch with an empty pizza box and virtual trophies, you might realize… there’s no real life left.But that promotion to Division 1—PRICELESS.

Player career mode as usual littered with bugs and feels hastily thrown together. I don't even understand why you would take stuff OUT of a re-skin of last years title, even if it's something as minimal as celebrations.You can't have a five star weak foot anymore. It's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ offline experience, why are you just randomly hamstringing players and taking things away?Manager career is so overly convoluted and filled with crap that it's bloated and a complete pain to organise and keep control of. Youth tournaments, individual scout assignments, and now player roles like we're playing Football Manager when in reality it does very little to actually affect the players in game.Youth players like goalkeepers have 18 diving or similarly low stats for attributes they should possess if they're a genuine prospect in that position. How the hell can you train a seventeen-year-old prospect to get a respectable level of diving before they're too old to be in the youth team anymore?The squad role, tactic, and position selection in manager career is so convoluted and confusing for no reason at all. It's all concealed in options hidden behind other options, and makes it a mind-bending chore for a new player to work their way around. There's reviews of people refunding the game after not being able to understand how to operate it and thinking it's bugged.Teams just get progressively worse and never seem to sign players for positions needed, and after a few seasons you'll notice top teams like Bayern or Real Madrid using players sub-75 players in their starting eleven. The AI model for CPU transfers is just bollocks, and eventually Europe's elite stop becoming elite, despite their overwhelming financial advantages over lower teams.The training plans for your team is such a horrible system and even if you leave it automated, your players will eventually just lose sharpness almost entirely. It would be absolutely amazing if this completely unneeded and added chore was removed. You receive constant e-mails about players lacking sharpness or energy every two days, constantly pulling you out of your simming.I fell for the same nonsense again and purchased FC25, hoping that the single player experience would at least be a tad bit more enjoyable this year around but obviously not.

I picked up the game on early access, expecting it to be another year of frustration due to bad gameplay and a lot of bugs, but I was very pleasantly surprised, as I encountered only a couple of minor bugs that are not in the gameplay itself, where they should least be. I watched the trailers for the game itself, as well as the things that were added in the new game, thinking that EA is trying to trick the players again in order to sell us another half-baked product that will annoy us for the next year, but this time everything you saw on trailers and on EA's website it is actually in the game and everything works as it should, who would have thought? A great game with all the bugs from previous years fixed. As for the gameplay itself, and in this game the gameplay is really the most important thing, I am very satisfied. It is much harder and more realistic to play, considering that players can no longer just turn around and make an accurate pass or kick from 30 meters and score a goal, but it is very important to use new mechanics in the tactics that the game provides, i.e. set up tactics the way that suits us best and set the players' roles. The ball has more realistic physics, goalkeepers don't make mistakes, they defend as they should, they are neither too good nor too bad, but just right. It took me about 10-14 days to get used to the new game, and EA IQ helped me a lot in that, but believe me, once you get used to it, it's fun to play. As far as the single player modes are concerned, you have options for additional realism, if you include the effect of the wind on the ball or the effect of the pitch on the ball and players, so that the impression is like watching a game on TV. As for me, I have nothing but praise for EA FC 25 and thank them for finally listening to the players. I hope that will be the case in the future as well. 10/10 rating from me.

EA Sports FC 25 Review: “It's Like Ordering Pizza and Getting a Salad”Alright, so EA Sports FC 25. The rebranded FIFA, but without the FIFA. What’s the difference? Well, it’s kind of like Pepsi changing its name to “Pepsi Liquid” and expecting people to get hyped. Spoiler: it’s still Pepsi.Let’s start with the gameplay. If you’ve played FIFA in the last, oh I don’t know, decade, congratulations—you’ve pretty much played EA Sports FC 25. The players still move like they’ve just discovered the concept of ankles, and the passing system is more indecisive than I am in a Taco Bell drive-thru. Dribble mechanics? Sure, you can dribble, but most of the time it feels like the ball is allergic to your feet.The graphics are... fine. If you squint, you might think you're watching a real match. But then again, if you squint hard enough, you might mistake a brick wall for a Monet painting. The sweat on players' faces looks more like they've just been sprayed with a garden hose than actual effort. I mean, I’m not expecting photo-realism here, but come on, is it too much to ask that Lionel Messi doesn’t look like a wax figure melting in the sun?Career Mode has all the excitement of watching paint dry, but slower. It’s like EA took all the energy from it and decided, "Nah, let’s save that for Ultimate Team where people actually spend money." Speaking of which—yes, Ultimate Team is back, and it’s still a casino disguised as a football game. EA Sports FC 25 Review: A Step Forward or Just a Sidestep?EA Sports FC 25, the latest installment in the long-running football simulation series, has been met with both anticipation and skepticism. As a successor to the FIFA series, it carries the weight of its predecessor's legacy while attempting to carve out its own identity. Here's a comprehensive review, breaking down key aspects of the game and rating them on a scale from 0 to 5.**Gameplay Mechanics – 4/5**The core gameplay of EA Sports FC 25 remains largely familiar, which is both its strength and weakness. The tactical layer introduced in this edition adds depth to the on-pitch action, allowing for a more strategic approach to matches. The improved HyperMotion technology enhances the realism of player movements and interactions, providing a more authentic representation of the sport.Graphically, EA Sports FC 25 offers incremental improvements over its predecessors. The player models and stadiums are detailed and vibrant, but there are no groundbreaking enhancements. The weather effects, such as wind and rain, add a nice touch of realism to the matches, although these are not present in online modes due to balancing reasons.Career Mode has received a welcome refresh, with more customization options for board expectations, training plans, and match tactics. This allows players to have greater control over their team's development and strategy. The addition of weather effects in offline modes also contributes to a more immersive experience.Rush Mode is a standout feature in EA Sports FC 25. This 5v5 mode offers a high-energy, fast-paced alternative to the traditional 11v11 gameplay. It's a fun, engaging mode that lasts just 7 minutes per match, making it an excellent choice for quick gaming sessions. The unified progression design with the season pass adds a rewarding element to the mode.While EA Sports FC 25 introduces some new features, the overall sense is that the game relies on refinements rather than revolutionary changes. The series' annual release cycle may contribute to this feeling of familiarity, as there is limited time for the development team to implement significant overhauls.EA Sports FC 25 is a competent football simulation game that will satisfy fans of the series. It makes some positive strides in gameplay and mode variety but falls short of being a transformative entry in the franchise. The game is most enjoyable for those who appreciate the nuances of football strategy and don't mind the lack of major innovations.In conclusion, EA Sports FC 25 is a solid, if not spectacular, addition to the football gaming landscape. It polishes the formula rather than reinventing it, and while some may find this approach lacking, others will enjoy the familiar gameplay with just enough tweaks to keep things interesting. Whether it's a step forward or merely a sidestep, EA Sports FC 25 is sure to provide countless hours of entertainment to football enthusiasts around the globe.

I'm backJust when I think it's over, a cool EA PR man provides ya slav boy with a review copy of EA Sports FC 25 (very tenk you for this) and I'm back at it again, grinding for some smexy cards and doing SBCs for fun.For my review, I'll only be talking about the changes to , cuz that's the mode I main. And like every year, there is good and bad, but so far, I really like how the gameplay feels, despite it being a tiny bit clunky.I'm in love with this year. Brainless pressure leaves gaps in your defense, as does using a midfielder while relying on the AI of your defenders to do the rest. Defending takes actual skill now. So, learn how to play, or heck, who am I to stop you from getting filled up if that is your kink? Also, you can commit an intentional foul (drag them to the ground), which, if used wisely, can zap the momentum from your opponent's attack.But we all know attack is more sexy, so is there any new additions?We got (didn't play the previous game, so it's new to me), a super skill-reliant gameplay mechanic, but if you spend some time learning how to use it, you may end up ripping defenses open like Indian food me. There's also , it's somewhere between manual and assisted, allowing more control over where you place your ballsBut delivering a precise pass in space or removing the cobwebs from the goal's corner aren't the only gameplay changes. , a staple of for years, were removed last year. Instead, we got . So far, I'm loving how they affect the gameplay in a more meaningful way than traits did. Each has two levels, base and gold, making the difference between a master header and an apprentice easily noticeable. PlayStyles just give players more personality and their strengths stood out more, at least to me.However, to me, the biggest improvement this year is . Now, you may say my IQ is that of a potato for playing this game year after year, but vodka is made from potatoes, so who is the real loser here? Anyway, FC IQ. This is just a fancy term for —roles a player will perform on the pitch. How well, well, that depends on the familiarity the player has with the assigned role, either none, a + (master) and ++ (world-class).The concept is indeed amazing, but the execution bit lacking depth, for now at least. I still love what is here tho. Each role has pros and cons, affecting how the player acts on the pitch. I hope EA expand this system further, adding more options for players to use in making their team's tactics.Do note that This fixes the possibility that any player can play in any position/role without issue, and I love it. I'm tired of seeing out-of-position players perform as good as someone who has dedicated their whole career to that one spot. No, a LB with no experience playing at CB should not play excellent there.I'm currently rocking a sexy Yugoslavia team, with a sturdy 5 at-the-back, with fullbacks pushing up whenever the team goes into attack mode, providing great support on the wings.But I gotta talk about for short, a system It's yet another thing that was introduced in the previous entry, but I just now got to play with it. And my GOD!!! This is it! This is what people who don't want meta crap dreamed for. My Yugoslavia Elite dream is now possible, as EVOs released during the year will offer me a way to improve my non-meta players and maybe find some hidden gems.I've heard that compared to last year, EVO has improved, specifically the restrictions and requirements a bit more relaxed now, so that's nice. I've already boosted four different poor players to good card, all for FREE. One EVO required coins, so expect some in the future will too, but it also gave my Moro dude an insane stat boost and a ++ Role. But so far, I'm bricked anytime I see a new EVO. I hope they let us use an EVO more than once, or change our pick. EA, just make it fun, please.But what about the grind?Squad Battles only has 12 games, each half lasts 4 minutes (used to be 6), and the rewards are better too. Now, while I do like the changes to UT Champs, I can see why many don't. There are only 5 qualifying games, which is more punishing for less skilled players. IMO, they should keep the 15 games (went from 20 to 15) for the weekend league but up the qualification games to 10 like it was. As for Division Rivals, it also got some new/old changes. You now earn points for rewards, 15 for level 1 rewards and 45 for level 2 rewards. So, about 15 wins for best rewards a division offers. And they are much better now, considering from Div 4 onward for rank 2 each week you get a TOTW player.So, overall, I do like these grind overhauls. It doesn't feel too overwhelming anymore nor does my effort go unrewarded. And since there are more untradeable rewards now, EA finally gave us a way to store untradeable duplicates, say hello to Now we have a convenient way to store and use dupes in SBCs instead of pointlessly discarding them.The new mode is not my jam tho. It's basically Volta, a 5v5 game mode, where defense is only a suggestion and people don't seem to know that it allows you to pass the ball to others. So, I suggest playing with friends, not randos, will probably be more enjoyable. The mode does lack rewards and incentives for me to want to play it. Yeah, there are some objectives, but eh, not really worth the grind imo, maybe for an EVO or two? We shall see...Now a bit of complaining.The menus... The UI... The heck is this? It just feels weird to control, and I hope we see an improvement in the next game. This list-type menu just doesn't work, at least for me. Too much wasted action and it's unintuitive, simple as that. Before we had clear and easy to understand menus. But now, I guess minimalism and all that took their toll, because this is just bad UI and UX design.There are also some weird menu bugs too. I often got locked out of doing anything, the game just froze, and so on, so had to restart quite a bit. And the controller issues (see my guide below) that are still present since day 1 kinda gave many people a sour taste, especially those who bought the game for Early Access.So, yeah, that's all there is to say. I love the game, people who know me know this is my favorite game of all time. I'm not a super football nerd either, I just like doing the SBC stuff, playing with unique cards/teams, and the grind/gameplay loop is fun to me. Why? I dunno, I like to play with balls I guess.With all of that said, I'm gonna head off now—my Yugoslavia brethren are calling.
